title: Equities Tumble After Caterpillar Misses, Nvidia Cuts Guidance
text:
Shutterstock photo Monday, January 28, 2019, 12:31 PM, EST NASDAQ Composite -1.24% Dow -1.27% S&P 500 -1.05% Russell 2000 -0.36% NASDAQ Advancers: 868 Decliners: 1403 Today's Volume (from friday) -0.55% Crude $51.77 -$1.92 , Gold $1301.70 +$3.60 , VIX 19.65 +2.20. Market Movers CAT down 8.6%, earnings NVDA down 14%, cut guidance GES down 16.25% CEO departure VALE down 15.75%, suspends dividend & buyback following dam break Chris's Commentary The market closed flat to slightly higher last week marking one of the best starts to the year in over 3 decades. The Dow, Nasdaq Composite and Russell 2000 inched higher for the 5th week in a row while the S&P 500 Index closed lower by less than 0.25%. As of Friday's close, the year-to-date return for the Dow was +6%, the Nasdaq Composite was up nearly +8%, the S&P 500 up +6.3% and the Russell 2000 Index climbed nearly +10%. The Federal Government ended the shutdown (albeit temporarily) which is a positive, but the repercussions of that shutdown are still being debated. S&P Global Ratings estimated that the partial shutdown cost the U.S. economy over $6 billion which is more than the estimated cost of the so called "border wall" for the U.S. southern border. All eleven S&P 500 sectors are lower with 6 sectors down over 1%. Tech is the worst down 1.5% followed by Communications down 1.3%, Health Care 1.25%, Industrials down 1.25% and Energy down 1.2%. Crude oil trades lower by 3.25%, but is still up 14.6% for the year. Gold trades higher while the dollar moves lower. The yield on the 10-yr has decreased to 2.74%. Earnings season for the quarter is underway and though it is early, with 114 members of the S&P 500 having reported, we have seen an average upside beat of over 1.45% for the S&P 500 as a whole. The quarterly earnings growth rate for the index has popped 13% while the sales growth rate is now nearly 5.5%. The Financial sector, with 35/68 members reporting so far, have posted the most noticeable negative comp with the average miss to the downside of -0.75%. Over 130 members of the S&P 500 are expected to report this week. We will get a heavy dose of Tech and Industrial reports to sort through, including such market movers AAPL, BA, MMM, QCOM, MSFT, FB, TSLA & AMZN. Bloomberg had a good note out today on market breadth . Stating that the Friday's gain in the S&P 500 kept the index above its 50 day moving average (~2612), which is a key, short term level of support. "While many market watchers have noted the breadth thrust, and the outperformance of small- and mid-cap stocks, large caps are holding their own, too. The equity benchmark's cumulative advance-decline line is approaching its previous record set in September, and a few more days of broad gains would push it to a new high. Let's see if today's negative start to the week will break this trend. Below is the economic calendar for the week. Tuesday, January 29 7:45 Retail Economist/Goldman Chain Store 8:30 Wholesale Inventories 8:55 Redbook Chain Store 9:00 Case-Shiller Home Price Index 10:00 Consumer Confidence 16:30 API Crude Inventories Wednesday, January 30 7:00 MBA Mortgage Purchase Applications 8:15 ADP Employment Report 8:30 GDP (advance) 8:30 GDP Chain Price (advance) 10:00 Pending Home Sales 10:30 DOE Crude Inventories 14:00 FOMC Announcment 14:30 Jerome Powell press conference Thursday, January 31 7:30 Challenger Job Cuts 8:30 Initial Jobless Claims 8:30 Continuing Claims 8:30 Personal Income 8:30 Personal Spending 9:45 Bloomberg Consumer Comfort 10:30 EIA Natural Gas Inventories Friday, February 1 8:30 Average Hourly Earnings 8:30 Average Weekly Hours 8:30 Nonfarm Payrolls 8:30 Unemployment Rate 9:45 Manufacturing PMI 10:00 Construction Spending 10:00 ISM Manufacturing Index 10:00 Michigan Consumer Sentiment (Final) Sector Recap

Brian's Technical Take
With all the events, earnings, and economic data expected this week, at the top of my focus list is Wednesday's FOMC and specifically the Fed 's statement and Jay Powell's Q&A regarding QT. Reminiscent of their about face on rates in Q4, it looks like the committee is quickly changing its tune from just one month ago when the Chairman said the balance sheet reduction program was on autopilot. The devil will be in the details and while prior communications have been confusing, the "hopium" crowd may get served. For the seventh consecutive session the S&P 500 is consolidating around the upper end of our expected resistance zone (2,631 - 2,643) where a cluster of technicals resides including Fibonacci retracements/projections, moving averages, and the prior pivot lows made in October and November. A number of headlines are being attributed to today's weakness and I would add it is the third consecutive week the SPX is starting off in the red. The prior two occurrences were the only red days for the week. The sideways consolidation is taking place in a ~60 point range which suggests a breakdown below the 2,610/15 support carries a measured move down to the 2,550 level. This equates to a 38.2% retracement of the entire four-week uptrend and if it happens could be an opportune time for cash on the sidelines to get back in the game.

We have a busy economic week ahead highlighted by NonFarm Payrolls on Friday, Consumer Confidence on Tuesday and the FOMC meeting mid-week. Any one of these items can spook the market or help send us higher.
